interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The retrieved guideline discusses using a risk-adapted pathway based on PI-RADS score, PSA density, and prior biopsy status. It states, "In a contemporary series of biopsies, the likelihood of finding a csPCa after follow-up biopsy after a diagnosis of atypical small acinar proliferation and high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia (PIN) was only 6-8% - not significantly different from follow-up biopsies after a negative biopsy." This suggests that the decision depends on risk factors like PSA density and PI-RADS score.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
EXPERT-STRUCTURED, your bid of BIOPSY p(biopsy) = 0.53 is uncertain, and the guideline treats the PI-RADS score and PSA density as key risk factors. The guideline suggests that a risk-based pathway can avoid biopsy in low-risk profiles, which is what this patient's PSA density and PI-RADS score might suggest. The guideline requires the patient's prior biopsy status to be established to determine the appropriate pathway. The guideline needs the documented prior grade of the prior biopsy to determine if the patient falls into a low-risk category.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE
previous_notes - the documented grade of the prior biopsy: at ISUP 2 or above the guideline sends him to treatment, not to more tissue; if it is unrecorded the indication stands
radiology_report - whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study: unchanged does not support re-sampling, new or larger does
